title: Fluid Mechanics
standard_code: Physics 2, Quarter 3: Periodic Motion and Fluid Mechanics
standard_text: Fluid mechanics: density and pressure; fluid statics (pressure with depth, Pascal's principle, Archimedes' principle and buoyancy); fluid dynamics (the continuity equation and Bernoulli's principle); viscosity and surface tension. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Physics 2, Quarter 3)
meta_desc: Free Physics 2 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 3): pressure in fluids, Pascal's and Archimedes' principles, flow and Bernoulli's principle, viscosity and surface tension. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pressure in a fluid at depth h is P = P₀ + ρgh. Pascal's principle says pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally, the basis of hydraulic lifts. Archimedes' principle: the buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced fluid.

For a fluid flowing through a pipe, A₁v₁ = A₂v₂: the fluid speeds up where the pipe narrows. Bernoulli's principle: where a fluid moves faster, its pressure is lower, which helps explain lift on airplane wings. Viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow.

Example

Extra pressure 10 m under water (ρ = 1,000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²)?

ρgh

Answer: 98,000 Pa

Example

A hose is narrowed to half its area. Water speed?

A₁v₁ = A₂v₂

Answer: it doubles

Common mistakes

  • Thinking pressure depends on the shape of the container.
  • Thinking faster flow means higher pressure.
  • Forgetting atmospheric pressure in total pressure.

faq.q: Why do your ears hurt when you dive deep?
faq.a: The water pressure increases with depth.

faq.q: How do airplane wings get lift?
faq.a: Air moves faster over the curved top, lowering the pressure there.
